paper.title_en: Entropy-Prescription Dependence of the Thermodynamic Topology of Charged Rotating Black Holes with Scalar Hair
paper.abstract_en: A thorough investigation of the thermodynamics of charged rotating black holes with scalar hair (CR-SH BHs) constructed by the Newman-Janis algorithm (NJA) is conducted in this study with a special focus on comparing three entropy formulations, such as Bekenstein-Hawking, Barrow, and logarithmic-corrected entropy. The analysis is performed in a canonical ensemble at fixed charge, angular momentum, and hair parameter, which leads to a closed form M(S, J, q, s) and verifies that the first law of thermodynamics and corresponding Smarr relation close identically. The conjugate temperature is fixed for the first law itself, $T_X = (\partial M/\partial S_X)_{J,q,s}$ for each entropy prescription, so that free energy, heat capacity and topological analysis are mutually consistent with each framework. The logarithmic corrections introduced in entropy formulations correspond to the quantum thermal fluctuations and become more pronounced in smaller BHs. Both Bekenstein-Hawking and Barrow entropies yield a topological charge 0, while the logarithmic entropy gives $-1$, indicating that the topological classification is sensitive to the entropy prescription. The heat capacity shows a single Davies divergence in both Bekenstein-Hawking and Barrow entropies, whereas logarithmic corrected entropy yields no divergence or pair of divergences bounding a narrow window of positive heat capacity. This change of class across prescriptions reflects the sensitivity of the topological classification to the adopted entropy functional and should not be interpreted as a phase transition of a single BH system.
